claim:
Let \(d\gamma=(2\pi)^{-1}e^{-|x|^2/2}\,dx\) on \(\mathbb R^2\), and let \(T_\gamma(K)=\int_K u\,d\gamma\), where \((\Delta-x\cdot\nabla)u=-1\) in \(K\) and \(u=0\) on \(\partial K\). For every nonzero smooth \(2\pi\)-periodic function \(f\) satisfying \(f(\theta+\pi)=f(\theta)\) and \(\int_0^{2\pi}f(\theta)\,d\theta=0\), let \(K_\varepsilon\) have support function \(h_\varepsilon(\theta)=1+\varepsilon f(\theta)\) for sufficiently small \(|\varepsilon|\). Then \(\operatorname{Per}(K_\varepsilon)=2\pi\) exactly, and if \(f(\theta)=\sum_{k\ge2,\ k\ \mathrm{even}}(a_k\cos k\theta+b_k\sin k\theta)\), then
\[
\left.\frac{d^2}{d\varepsilon^2}T_\gamma(K_\varepsilon)\right|_{\varepsilon=0}
=\frac{\sqrt e-1}{2\sqrt e}\sum_{\substack{k\ge2\\ k\ \mathrm{even}}}\left[2-(\sqrt e-1)(k^2+2\lambda_k)\right](a_k^2+b_k^2)<0,
\]
where \(\lambda_k=F_k'(1)\) and
\[
F_k(r)=\frac{r^k\,{}_1F_1(k/2;k+1;r^2/2)}{{}_1F_1(k/2;k+1;1/2)}.
\]
Thus the unit disk is strictly second-order stable in every nontrivial smooth centrally symmetric Euclidean-perimeter-preserving support direction for Gaussian torsional rigidity. This is a local second-variation result only; it does not prove the global fixed-perimeter maximization problem.

correctness.rationale: For a smooth support path, Cauchy perimeter is exactly constant. The support-to-radial conversion gives the quadratic radial correction \(-f'{}^2/2\). Standard smooth-domain elliptic differentiation yields homogeneous OU equations for the first two Eulerian derivatives; expansion of the moving Dirichlet boundary gives their exact boundary data. Separation of variables gives the regular Kummer mode \(F_k\), and positivity of the Kummer series yields \(\lambda_k>k\). Angular orthogonality isolates the constant second-order mode, while the moving Gaussian collar contributes the remaining explicit term. The resulting coefficient is \((\sqrt e-1)/(2\sqrt e)[2-(\sqrt e-1)(k^2+2\lambda_k)]\), strictly negative for every even \(k\ge2\). The packaged verifier checks the algebraic normalization, radial expansion, sample Kummer values, and all-mode sign margin; finite checks are not used as the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The closest directly relevant 2026 papers establish Brunn--Minkowski failures, ball-only interpolation statements, and an explicit first-order disk calculation, but the lead paper expressly leaves the centrally symmetric fixed-perimeter maximization question open and says it does not prove the exact first variation. The new statement instead computes the full smooth centrally symmetric support-direction Hessian at the unit disk and proves every admissible mode is negative. Exact published-finding corpus searches for the Gaussian torsion Hessian, Kummer/Fourier formulation, fixed-perimeter local maximizer formulation, and aliases returned no covering record. Classical Laplace-torsion second variations are analogous but do not imply the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck coefficients.
residual_risks: An unindexed or terminology-mismatched shape-calculus paper could contain the same weighted second variation; this is a residual originality risk because classical Laplace-torsion analogues exist.
The lead source open question is global, while the present theorem is only a smooth local second-variation result at the unit disk.
No claim is made that strict negativity of every smooth direction alone supplies a uniform Banach-space local-maximizer theorem.
